subject: FinPrime: Multi-region failover commitments and RPO offsets
messages:
From: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@finprime.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: support@finprime.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-region failover obligations and RPO offsets

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. As we formalize the SOW with our legal and risk teams, a couple of points came up that we need clarity on:

- FinPrime operates a warm-standby in APAC to meet regional latency targets. We understand Redwood's standard failover SLA is 99.95% availability with RTO 15 minutes and RPO 5 minutes for active-active customers. For customers with cross-region warm-standby (not full active-active), can Redwood provide a formal exception carve-out for RTO/RPO when activating a standby region?
- When an activation is required (regional outage), who owns the network cutover steps vs. Redwood’s service failover? Specifically we need a clear responsibilities matrix: FinPrime network ops will route BGP and update DNS, but we want Redwood to own the application-side warmup, KV cache priming, and prefix cache replay.
- If the RTO/RPO during a standby activation differs materially from the standard SLA, can Redwood propose an offset (e.g., pro-rated credits or a documented make-good) and a measured rollback plan?

I've attached our DR questionnaire (FinPrime-DR-Questionnaire.pdf). Ideally we could get a short write-up from Redwood by Friday outlining proposed responsibilities and any quantitative RTO/RPO offsets so we can include them in the SOW.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our legal team is pushing to close the SOW next week.

Regards,
Alice Zhao
Head of Infrastructure
FinPrime

---
Attachment: FinPrime-DR-Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)
From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Multi-region failover obligations and RPO offsets

Team — forwarding FinPrime's questionnaire and ask. They want explicit ownership and an RTO/RPO offset proposal for warm-standby activations in APAC. Key points to address:

1) Operational responsibilities matrix (network cutover vs application warmup).
2) Measured RTO/RPO we can commit to for warm-standby activations and how that differs from our standard 15/5 baseline. Be conservative and include any assumptions (sequence length, KV cache warmup time, model cold-start penalties).
3) Compensation or credit construct if activation exceeds the carved-out RTO window.
4) Process for runbook handoff and verification (who toggles prefixes, expected lead time).

Marissa — can you draft the proposed matrix and a one-page runbook excerpt we can send back to Alice? Karthik — need an engineering estimate for warm-start timelines (KV cache replay, concurrency ramp) and any mitigations (pre-warming, prioritized background cache replay).

We should keep this customer-friendly but explicit — legal will want precise language. Target internal draft by EOD Wed so we can respond Friday.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@finprime.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region failover obligations and RPO offsets

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear questionnaire. Attached is a proposed fallback responsibilities matrix (proposed-fallback-matrix.xlsx) and a short runbook excerpt (redwood-runbook-draft.md) that spells out activation steps we would perform vs. steps we'd expect FinPrime to own. Summary here: 

- Pre-activation: FinPrime performs BGP/DNS cutover (we list exact prefix changes and expected TTLs). Redwood performs continuous KV-prefix snapshotting and keeps a prioritized cache replay queue for customer-critical prefixes.
- Activation: For warm-standby, estimated RTO = 25 minutes (best-effort) and estimated RPO = 10 minutes. These are derived assuming average KV cache priming of ~7 minutes for hot prefixes and model instance spin-up of ~3–5 minutes on reserved capacity.
- Mitigations: We recommend optional pre-warm window (10 minutes prior to planned maintenance) where FinPrime signals intent and Redwood starts prioritized replay; this reduces RTO to ~12–15 minutes.
- Credit construct: If an unplanned activation exceeds the carved-out 25-minute RTO by more than 30 minutes, Redwood proposes a pro-rated credit equal to 1.5x the token-based usage for the affected period (to be reflected as an SOW addendum).

Please see the attachments for the detailed step list and the exact phrasing we can include in the SOW. If this aligns, Kimberly and I can work with your legal team to produce redlined language.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: proposed-fallback-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), redwood-runbook-draft.md (text/markdown)
From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@finprime.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region failover obligations and RPO offsets

Alice — following up with formal proposal attached (runbook excerpt and fallback matrix). Short summary for your SOW: 

- For customers with warm-standby topology, Redwood will commit to a documented activation RTO of 25 minutes and RPO of 10 minutes as a carve-out from the standard 15/5 SLA baseline; these values assume FinPrime completes the network cutover tasks within the documented lead times.
- Redwood ownership during activation: application warmup (model instance readiness), prioritized KV cache replay, and traffic validation hooks.
- FinPrime ownership: BGP/DNS cutover, edge firewall rules, and confirmation of routing propagation. 
- Pre-warm option: when FinPrime can provide a 10-minute pre-warm signal, Redwood will reduce activation RTO to 12–15 minutes (operationally verified).
- Credit mechanic: unplanned activations that exceed 25-minute RTO by >30 minutes trigger a pro-rated usage credit (detailed in the attached SOW language).

If this is acceptable, we can bake the exact paragraphs into an SOW addendum and route for signatures. Let me know if you want us to also draft the redline.

Thanks again for the close coordination — we want the SOW to reflect operational reality and minimize surprise during an actual failover.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
